messages:
Maya: quick sync to lock Q2 observability console scope. Two customer-driven asks: per-route cost breakdown (tokens -> $) and actionable error analytics for inference failures. We also need tracing hooks to link errors to requests. Can we put engineering bounds + acceptance gates here today?
Tony: short eng summary: dashboards + cost-explorer = ~3 sprints (backend + query layers + UI). Tracing envelope + sampling = ~2 sprints if we reuse runtime hooks. Biggest unknown is cost-attribution accuracy and the aggregation pipeline.
Zara: SRE: tracing can spike cardinality. Recommend envelope-level telemetry (no full-span capture) and async export. Default sampling 0.1% prod, 100% on canary. Also add quota-aware backoff.
Sophie: design POV: MVP = 1) single summary dashboard, 2) lightweight cost-explorer w/ filters (model, route, customer), 3) compact error analytics panel (top error types, trend). Keep interactions minimal; avoid multi-screen flows at launch.
Eli: ops ask: need alerts for per-route cost or error-rate spikes + runbook + CSV export for billing reconciliation. These must be part of acceptance.
Tony: implementation note: runtime can emit a compact trace envelope. Example we can start instrumenting:
```json
{
  "trace_id": "<uuid>",
  "model": "gpt-j-16k",
  "route": "generate/text",
  "tokens": 124,
  "gpu_ms": 42,
  "error": null,
  "sample_rate": 0.001
}
```
Zara: that envelope looks fine. Export path: async -> queue -> telemetry pipeline. Enforce redaction prior to export. Include sample_rate field so downstream can scale estimates.
Maya: proposed tradeoff: MVP = envelope-only (no full spans), default sample_rate=0.1% prod, canary 100%. Show per-route estimated $/1k tokens in UI rather than exact billing. Anyone object?
Tony: agree. For cost model we'll calculate estimate = tokens * per_token_cost + infra_overhead. Aggregation and batching required to avoid emitting per-token metrics at high volume.
Eli: gating for GA suggestion: 1) dashboard shows 24h for baseline routes; 2) envelope processing latency <5s end-to-end on canary; 3) cost estimate error <10% on representative workload; 4) alerts validated with injected spikes.
Sophie: UX acceptance: persistent filter state, quick CSV export, and error drilldown showing top-5 errors + one redacted payload sample per error type. Low effort, high impact.
Maya: action items: Tony -> detailed eng plan + sprint breakdown by EOD; Zara -> sampling + perf test plan; Sophie -> mockups for single-page drilldowns; Eli -> customer comms & canary list. I'll draft acceptance gates doc. Sync 10:30 PT. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: notice: telemetry pipeline quota enforcement starts 2026-04-01. See https://internal.redwood/telemetry-quotas
Tony: will include quota-aware fallback (batching, aggregated metrics, backpressure).
Zara: one security acceptance: error analytics must include top-5 stack traces and a single redacted payload sample per error type. Validate PII redaction before export.
Maya: final MVP scope lock: summary dashboard + cost-explorer + CSV export, tracing envelope (sampled, async), error analytics (top5 + redacted payloads), alerts + runbook. If any blockers surface, ping me. Thanks all.
